cases.title: Apartment complex brand with a given-name element
cases.why: A residential brand built from a given name and 하우스 ('house'); moving in is predicated of a building.

ambiguity.note: 입주하다 ('move in') takes a building as its place complement.

cases.title: 박카스 starting with the surname 박
cases.why: A drink brand beginning with 박; the brand is a product, not a person.

ambiguity.note: Drinking a bottle of a beverage.

cases.title: 하린이 신제품을 소개했다: a brand or a person
cases.why: 하린 is a given name and a plausible brand; introducing a new product is something a company or an individual presenter does.

ambiguity.note: Presenting a product fits both a person on stage and a company; there is no head noun or honorific.

cases.title: 라온 as a company or a person, bare subject
cases.why: 라온 is a modern given name and a very common company-name element; bidding is something a firm or an individual can do.

ambiguity.note: No 건설, 주식회사 or 씨 follows 라온, so a firm and an individual bidder are both defensible.

cases.title: Brand name directly before a product noun
cases.why: A given-name-like word directly before a product noun is a brand name.

ambiguity.note: No topic marker follows 서진 and the product noun 에어프라이어 completes the name.

cases.title: Fictional brand 최강 치킨 containing two surname syllables
cases.why: 최강 ('the strongest') is built from the surnames 최 and 강. In the fictional brand name 최강 치킨 no person is mentioned.

ambiguity.note: 'Opened a new store' is something a business does.

cases.title: 이마트 starting with the surname 이
cases.why: A retail chain name beginning with 이 plus 마트 ('mart').

ambiguity.note: Shopping for groceries 'at X' selects a store.

cases.title: Fictional firm 박앤이 세무회계 made of two surnames
cases.why: A firm name made of two surnames joined by 앤 ('and'), followed by a business description. No person is mentioned.

ambiguity.note: 'Called from X' with the business descriptor 세무회계 marks an office.

cases.title: 한샘 starting with the surname 한
cases.why: A furniture company whose name begins with the common surname syllable 한 plus a noun.

ambiguity.note: Ordering a sofa from a company.

cases.title: 한화 starting with the surname 한
cases.why: A conglomerate name beginning with the common surname 한, written like a one-syllable name plus a noun.

ambiguity.note: 'Built a new factory this year' is a corporate action.

cases.title: Fictional pharmacy 정직한 약국 starting with the surname syllable 정
cases.why: 정직한 means 'honest' and begins with 정; the business name is a descriptor plus 약국 ('pharmacy').

ambiguity.note: 'Closed on Sundays' describes a business.

cases.title: 현대자동차 starting with the syllable 현
cases.why: A company name beginning with the syllable 현 and ending with 자동차 ('automobile').

ambiguity.note: 'Announced a new car' is something a manufacturer does.

cases.title: 정관장 starting with the surname 정
cases.why: A ginseng brand beginning with 정 and ending in 관장 ('director').

ambiguity.note: A gift set is a product.

cases.title: 진라면 starting with the surname 진
cases.why: A noodle brand beginning with 진 plus 라면.

ambiguity.note: A packaged food discounted in a store.

cases.title: Law office whose name begins with surname-like syllables
cases.why: A firm name made of surname syllables joined by 앤 and ending in 법률사무소 ('law office') is an organization.

ambiguity.note: 법률사무소 is an institutional head noun, so the string is an organization.

cases.title: 오뚜기 starting with the surname 오
cases.why: A food company whose name begins with 오 and means a roly-poly toy.

ambiguity.note: 'Launched a new product' is a company action.

cases.title: Person acquiring a food company with her given name
cases.why: A person and a food company sharing a given name, linked by an acquisition predicate.

ambiguity.note: Acquiring a company takes an organization object; 식품 is an industry head noun.

cases.title: A person named 윤슬 who owns a cafe called 윤슬 카페
cases.why: A given name and a business named after it in one sentence: the first is the owner, the second the business.

ambiguity.note: 'Runs X' selects a business; the first token takes the topic marker as the subject.

cases.title: Given name with a topic marker before a product noun
cases.why: Partner of brand-appliance-without-particle: the topic particle 은 after the name separates the person from the product.

ambiguity.note: 은 marks 서진 as the topic and buyer.

cases.title: Person with 씨 running a pharmacy with the same given name
cases.why: The honorific 씨 selects the person; the pharmacy is a business named after the same syllables.

ambiguity.note: 씨 attaches to a person and 약국 is a business head noun.

cases.title: Person and a salad brand with the same given name
cases.why: A given name followed by 은 and a salad brand named after the same given name.

ambiguity.note: The topic-marked name is the orderer; the name followed directly by a menu noun is a brand.

cases.title: Person reviewing a bakery with the same given name
cases.why: A given name and a bakery brand with the same syllables.

ambiguity.note: The subject-marked name is the one who praises; 베이커리 is a business head noun, so the name before it is a bakery brand.

cases.title: Person and an electronics company with the same given name
cases.why: A person and a company named with his given name plus 전자 ('electronics').

ambiguity.note: The topic-marked name is the representative; 전자 is a company head noun.

cases.title: Person teaching at an academy with his given name
cases.why: A person and a private academy with the same given name.

ambiguity.note: 학원 is an institution head noun and 에서 강의한다 marks a workplace.

cases.title: Person and chicken restaurant with the same given name
cases.why: A restaurant brand named after a given name and the person with that name in one sentence.

ambiguity.note: 민준이가 is the name plus the informal name suffix 이 plus the subject marker 가; 치킨 is a business head noun, so 민준 치킨 is a restaurant.

cases.title: Person and construction firm with the same given name
cases.why: A given name and a company built on that name appear together; only the first is a person.

ambiguity.note: 건설 ('construction') is a company head noun and 에서 근무한다 marks the workplace.

cases.title: A person working at a firm named with two surnames
cases.why: The full name 김민수 and the fictional firm 박앤이 세무회계 share no characters, but both contain surname syllables. One is a person and the other an organization.

ambiguity.note: 'Works at X' with the locative 에서 marks the second as an employer; the first takes the topic marker.

cases.title: Elementary school named with a given name
cases.why: A school name that begins with a given-name-like word is an organization.
cases.text: 정민 초등학교는 금요일에 단축 수업을 한다.

ambiguity.note: 초등학교 is an institutional head noun.

cases.title: 신라면 starting with the surname 신
cases.why: A packaged-noodle brand beginning with 신 and followed by the common noun 라면.

ambiguity.note: Boiling and eating selects a food product.

cases.title: Given name with 선생님
cases.why: Partner of school-named-with-given-name: the same two syllables followed by 선생님 are a person.

ambiguity.note: 선생님 attaches to a person; the title stays outside the span.

cases.title: Trading company named with two-syllable name
cases.why: A two-syllable name followed by 물산 ('trading company') is a company.

ambiguity.note: 물산 is a company head noun and announcing a product is predicated of a company.

cases.title: Fictional cafe 윤슬 카페 containing the name-like word 윤슬
cases.why: 윤슬 is both a given name and a word for water glitter; as the name of a fictional cafe no person is meant.

ambiguity.note: 'Meet at X' with the head noun 카페 ('cafe') selects a venue.
